Default region of practical equivalence for treatment coefficients

Source: R/utils-posterior-decisions.R
default_rope.Rd

On identity links (gaussian, student, skew_normal) the region is +/- 0.1 pooled within-phase SD: the SD of observations around their case-by-phase means, so the treatment effect itself does not widen the region (the outcome SD is the fallback when it cannot be computed). On log and logit links it is +/- log(1.1), a 10\ multipliers are conventions, not substantive thresholds; supply a context-specific ROPE when one is known. Other links require explicit bounds on their own scale.

Usage

default_rope(data, family = "gaussian", response = "outcome")

Arguments

data

Processed data from process_scd_phases() (pass these rather than raw data or model$data). Without a phase column, as in model$data of a fit on coded columns, phases are recovered from the coded step columns (level_*, atd_*, treatment): each distinct combination of their values within a tier is one phase.

family

brms family name or family object.

response

Response column name.

Value

Numeric length-2 vector c(lower, upper) on the link scale.

Details

Phases are grouped within tiers (tier_vars()), so a case identifier repeated across studies or behaviors does not pool two series. Each run of a phase label within a tier is its own phase (A1 and A2 of a reversal design are separate), except in alternating-treatments designs, where all sessions of a condition form one phase.

Examples

default_rope(simulate_scd_data(n_cases = 3), "gaussian")
#> [1] -1.098565  1.098565
default_rope(simulate_scd_data(n_cases = 3), "poisson")
#> [1] -0.09531018  0.09531018
